findings.text: Routine update_srbds_msr provides a per CPU synchronization operation for SRBDS microcode control that leaves the control register untouched when the boot CPU is unaffected or virtualized or awaiting microcode or lacking control capability, and otherwise preserves unrelated control bits while setting or clearing the random data mitigation disable bit according to whether the retained mode is disabled or TSX off or full.

Routine update_gds_msr provides a per CPU synchronization operation for GDS microcode control that returns without register access in automatic and forced without microcode and missing microcode and hypervisor states, otherwise reads the microcode control register and sets the gather mitigation disable bit when disabled and clears it when full or full locked, writes it back, then rereads to detect ignored writes.

Routine gds_ucode_mitigated is a predicate reporting whether GDS is currently handled by microcode, true only when the retained mode is full or full locked and false in all other modes including disabled and automatic and missing microcode and forced and hypervisor dependent.

Handlers mds_cmdline with tsx_async_abort_parse_cmdline with mmio_stale_data_parse_cmdline provide boot commands for MDS and TAA and MMIO stale data that do nothing when the corresponding bug is absent on the boot CPU and reject missing option text as invalid, otherwise translating requests for disabled and full clearing and full clearing with SMT disabled into the retained mitigation enumeration and associated no SMT flag.

Handlers rfds_parse_cmdline with srbds_parse_cmdline with gds_parse_cmdline with l1d_flush_parse_cmdline provide boot commands for RFDS and SRBDS and GDS and L1D flush that validate option text and bug presence, then record disabled and enabled and forced requests into retained state, with SRBDS remembering a disable request for later selection and L1D enabling only an explicit on request while unrecognized text is ignored.

Routine should_mitigate_vuln defines attack vector policy for speculative execution issues where Spectre V1 depends only on the user to kernel vector, while Spectre V2 with Retbleed and L1TF and ITS depend on user to kernel or guest to host, Spectre V2 user depends on user to user or guest to guest, store bypass depends only on user to user, and VMSCAPE depends only on guest to host.

Routine should_mitigate_vuln defines attack vector policy for cross address space sampling issues where MDS and TAA and MMIO stale data and RFDS and SRBDS require mitigation when any of the four user kernel and guest host and user user and guest guest vectors is protected, while GDS adds an extra condition on SMT mitigations being active, and unknown bug identifiers warn and report no mitigation.

Models MDS mitigation as automatic choice resolved through attack vector policy into disabled or full clearing, later reconciled with shared buffer clearing desire and memory clear microcode support, surfaced through status text, and finally enforced by forcing buffer clearing capabilities and conditionally disabling SMT except on MSBDS only systems.

Models TAA mitigation with a distinct TSX disabled outcome when transactional memory is unavailable, otherwise automatic choice into disabled or buffer clearing with shared desire recording, later reconciliation that also demands TSX control microcode on MDS no systems, and enforcement through buffer clearing capabilities plus conditional SMT disable.

Models MMIO stale data mitigation where automatic choice becomes disabled or buffer clearing, shared desire is recorded only when MDS or TAA also affect the system, final state is reconciled with shared desire and fill buffer clear capability expressed either directly or through memory clear with L1D flush, and enforcement selects host plus virtual clearing or MMIO only virtual clearing and enables idle clearing and may disable SMT.

Models RFDS mitigation where automatic choice becomes disabled or register file clearing, shared desire is recorded only when the architecture reports that buffer clearing also clears the register file, final state is reconciled with shared desire and that same capability with a missing microcode outcome otherwise, and enforcement forces buffer clearing capabilities only in the clearing state.

Models SRBDS mitigation where automatic choice becomes disabled or full microcode, with later refinement to TSX disabled on MDS no systems without transactional memory and without MMIO exposure, to hypervisor dependent under virtualization, to missing microcode without control capability, and to disabled when requested off, all surfaced through status text and enforced by the per CPU control register update.

Models GDS mitigation with hypervisor dependent handling under virtualization, automatic choice into disabled or full, missing microcode handling without gather control capability unless forced, promotion from forced to full when microcode appears, locked full handling when the control register reports locked, per CPU enforcement through the disable bit, and a fallback that clears the AVX feature when forced without microcode.

Models two minimal mitigations where L1D flush defaults to disabled and only an explicit on request plus L1D flush hardware support enables a conditional flush on address space switch with an informational message, while Spectre V1 retains only a none versus automatic choice defaulted by build configuration and described by status text contrasting barrier coverage.

Retains small mode enumerations for MDS and TAA and MMIO and RFDS that each distinguish disabled and automatic and active clearing states plus distinct outcomes for missing microcode or TSX disabled where applicable, held in read only after init variables defaulted from build configuration.

Retains mode enumerations for SRBDS and GDS and L1D flush and Spectre V1 that distinguish disabled and automatic and full or on states plus specialized outcomes such as missing microcode and TSX off and hypervisor dependent and forced and locked full, with SRBDS and GDS defaulted from build configuration and L1D defaulting to disabled in init data.

A single shared flag for buffer clearing couples MDS with TAA with MMIO with RFDS so that selection in one mitigation can move the others toward clearing during their update phase, with MDS recording desire whenever active and TAA whenever not disabled and MMIO only with MDS or TAA exposure and RFDS only with register file clear capability.

Mitigation control variables for MDS with TAA with MMIO with RFDS with SRBDS with GDS with Spectre V1 live in read only after init storage and default to automatic when the matching build time mitigation option is enabled and to disabled otherwise, while L1D flush lives in init data defaulting to disabled and no SMT request flags default to false.

Disabling of simultaneous multithreading happens only while applying an active mitigation when either a per mitigation no SMT request was given or the global SMT mitigation mode is on, with MDS additionally exempting systems affected only by MSBDS, while GDS instead consults global SMT state during selection rather than forcing disable at apply time.

Progress from requested clearing to reported protection requires enumerated microcode capabilities, including memory clear for MDS and TAA and TSX control on MDS no systems for TAA and fill buffer clear or memory clear with L1D flush for MMIO and register file clear for RFDS and control capability for SRBDS and GDS, with failure diverting to missing microcode states that may still enforce clearing.

When the boot CPU reports a hypervisor, SRBDS and GDS selections move to a hypervisor dependent state with unknown protection rather than programming the control register, and their per CPU updates return early, while other mitigations here show no distinct virtual host handling beyond separate virtualized clearing capabilities.

Hazardous effects need care including a warning on unknown vulnerability identifiers and a one time warning when a GDS control write appears ignored from lock mismatch and a warning when locked control cannot be disabled and clearing of the AVX feature as a last resort when GDS is forced without microcode and irreversible SMT disabling during apply.

Hardware control uses register MSR_IA32_MCU_OPT_CTRL with disable bit RNGDS_MITG_DIS for SRBDS behavior and disable bit GDS_MITG_DIS with lock indicator GDS_MITG_LOCKED for GDS behavior, where setting a disable bit requests no microcode mitigation and clearing requests mitigation and lock forces locked full reporting.

Capability reporting uses arch cap bits ARCH_CAP_MDS_NO with ARCH_CAP_TSX_CTRL_MSR with ARCH_CAP_FB_CLEAR with ARCH_CAP_FBSDP_NO with ARCH_CAP_RFDS_CLEAR with ARCH_CAP_GDS_CTRL to indicate absence of MDS exposure and availability of TSX control and fill buffer clearing and propagation properties and register file clearing and gather control.

CPU identity uses feature indicators X86_FEATURE_MD_CLEAR with X86_FEATURE_FLUSH_L1D with X86_FEATURE_RTM with X86_FEATURE_HYPERVISOR with X86_FEATURE_SRBDS_CTRL with X86_FEATURE_AVX with X86_FEATURE_CLEAR_CPU_BUF variants and bug indicators X86_BUG_MDS with X86_BUG_TAA with X86_BUG_MMIO_STALE_DATA with X86_BUG_RFDS with X86_BUG_SRBDS with X86_BUG_GDS with Spectre and related speculation bug identifiers to gate each mitigation.

Each mitigation keeps a table mapping its retained mode to human readable status that contrasts vulnerable outcomes with active mitigation outcomes and distinguishes missing microcode and TSX disabled and hypervisor dependent cases, emitted through informational logging during update or apply.
